newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW:British Gas decision not marginal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW:British Gas decision not marginal.

text.p: British Gas Plc deputy chairman Philip Rogerson said on Thursday that the rejection of regulatory price controls proposed for its TransCo gas transmission operations "was not a marginal decision."

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Rogerson said the two sides had made little progress in weeks of talks, although the final decision to reject the controls was only made on Wednesday. "I am extremely disappointed," said Rogerson, who led British Gas's negotiating team. "It is very unfortunate that we have got some unrealistic proposals."

Rogerson said the talks foundered on a number of key issues, including Ofgas's approach to accounting for asset valuations and depreciation. He said Ofgas's assumptions on operating costs were also "nothing like" adequate.
Another sticking point was Ofgas's proposals for the "unbundling" of TransCo's gas storage operations.

"The proposals are wholly unclear. We don't know if the intention is to price control them and if so on what basis costs would be allowed, or on what basis they would be allowed to compete in a competitive market place," Rogerson said.
Rogerson said negotiations with Ofgas never got as far as British Gas outlining what it would have been ready to accept.

"It never got to that position. The regulator doesn't work on that basis," he said. The rejection is expected to lead to a lengthy inquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), which could last well into 1997, when British Gas is planning to demerge into two businesses, Transco and British Gas Energy, the U.K. gas supply business.
But Rogerson said the timetable for the spin-off will not be affected. He said the decision "does not create any uncertainty about the business to be demerged," British Gas Energy.
However, it does create further uncertainty for British Gas's hard-pressed shareholders. Shares in the group were down 6 pence at 193 by midmorning.

Rogerson said decisions on the dividend cannot be made until the uncertainty is cleared up. "The dividend is a matter we will look at at the appropriate time," Rogerson said, adding that the next opportunity will be full-year results due in February.

Rogerson also strongly criticised Ofgas's refusal to allow British Gas to see consultants' reports on which their decisions were based. "This hampered our ability to understand the logic of their proposals," he added.
